chapter_mission: Establish Ben's restlessness and the wrongness in the Force, launch the investigation via Luke's survey assignment, and depart Coruscant with the wrongness now directional.
chapter_turn: Ben moves from passive unease to active pursuit with institutional cover — the wrongness transforms from ambient background to a compass needle.

scene_plan.purpose: Establish the wrongness through physical failure in sparring — make it concrete and costly, not abstract meditation. Ground Ben's Lie (self-reliance as safety) in observable behavior.
Luke validates Ben's read of the wrongness and assigns the survey mission. Father and son communicate through mission briefings; neither acknowledges the choice to send Ben alone.
Ben bypasses the Jedi partner roster for Desh Rolan — self-reliance dressed as practicality. Departure turns the wrongness from ambient to directional, transforming retreat into unconscious pursuit.

relationship_turns.from: institutional distance — father-son filtered through rank and mission
relationship_turns.to: private alliance — Luke entrusts Ben with the wrongness investigation without closing the distance

relationship_turns.from: dormant contact — shared GAG history neither discusses
relationship_turns.to: operational partnership — Desh accepts the job without asking why Ben didn't call a Jedi

exit_vector: Ben in hyperspace, wrongness pulling not just pointing — active, not ambient. The chapter ends on unconscious pursuit disguised as a routine survey.
notes: H01 is planted in scene 2 (Luke's mission brief) and advanced in scene 3 (Ben acts on it by departing). R01 lands at the close of scene 3 — the wrongness acquires direction during hyperspace transit, which it shouldn't. The chapter's emotional spine is Ben's Lie (self-reliance as control) expressed through three escalating isolation choices: sparring alone, accepting the mission without suggesting backup, calling Desh instead of a Jedi. SP-A runs through all three scenes; merged SP3 (per D5) covers both the institutional distance from the Order in scenes 1-2 and Ben's relationship with Desh arriving in scene 3. Voice anchor: Zahn-style tight third-person interiority throughout; Ben's internal voice sharp and self-deprecating, never melodramatic. Anti-patterns at chapter level: do not describe the wrongness in visual/color terms (keep auditory/vibrational); do not resolve the father-son distance (that's the novel's long arc).
